focus: enforcement layer: parsers, guards, compiler, packager, pinned-prose check, canon and doctor reach

graphEvents.label: Which checks pin the current routing shape?
Per-mode ROUTER.md is unparseable by the replay

label: A packet-root ROUTER.md is invisible to the replay: findReferencedRouterDoc accepts only references/*.md (router-replay-lib.cjs:374) or the convention path references/smart-routing.md (:384), so a ROUTER.md at a packet root matches neither and any per-mode router file is unparseable by the component that verifies stage two.

Moving a packet machine block anywhere inside the same SKILL.md is safe for parseRouter: it extracts INTENT_SIGNALS and RESOURCE_MAP from the whole SKILL.md text (:397-403) with no section or order constraint, so an appendix parses identically and the report "may not be free" risk is resolvable with no tooling change at packet level.

The router-sync guard covers sk-code only: every leg is keyed to the SKCODE constant, SURFACES is [sk-code-ci, sk-code-skilled], hubPacketDirs walks SKCODE, and readSkillRouter reads <packet>/SKILL.md (:47), so sk-doc 14 packets, sk-design 4 and system-deep-loop 3 are outside the guard, which is why sk-doc 9 router-less packets pass unnoticed.

Leg 2 fails closed on a stage1-only hub: legSurfaceMap pushes a problem when SHARED_CONTROL_RESOURCES is empty (verify-router-sync.cjs:198-200, "so the parent-tier check would be vacuous") and requires each surface resourceMap to be non-empty, so a hub that legitimately delegates stage two to JSON breaks the leg even though the canon blesses router_state stage1-only.

JSON-only for hubs fails a frozen contract code rather than a style rule: root-router-contract.cjs freezes RRC-001 MISSING_ROOT_ROUTER, RRC-005 STAGE1_NONEMPTY and RRC-009 MISSING_PROSE_SECTION (:127-135) and check 12a runs that library against every hub (parent-skill-check.cjs:1787-1830), so deleting a hub ROUTER.md fails 12a with RRC-001 and a stage1-only hub must still ship empty maps under RRC-005.

The compiled-route compiler hashes the hub SKILL.md plus hub-router.json and mode-registry.json (build-artifacts.cjs:44-58), reads them from the .opencode mirror rather than .skilled, and does not hash packet SKILL.md; .skilled/skills/<hub> and .opencode/skills/<hub> are separate real directories with byte-identical files today for all four hubs, so restructuring must be written to both or the compiled route compiles old bytes.

package_skill.py pins the section name and three marker words: it requires an H2 named SMART ROUTING (:69, variants :79-80), requires discover_markdown_resources, _guard_in_skill and UNKNOWN_FALLBACK inside that section (:182-184) and validates it at :769, so a shrunk 8-to-12-line section survives only if those markers stay inside section 2.

check-rule-copies.js pins prose inside sk-code-review/SKILL.md: its EXTENSION_FLOORS block reads that file (:169-170) and its header states the pin exists so no repository extension can reword or drop a floor unseen (:18), so a readability pass over review must leave those lines byte-identical or change the pin in the same commit.

The reach diagnostic consumes the document JSON-only would delete: doctor-router-reach.yaml:64-65 takes stage-one vocabulary from .skilled/skills/*/graph-metadata.json and stage-two vocabulary from .skilled/skills/*/ROUTER.md, and the canon states the router is first-class at the hub root as ROUTER.md never at a nested path (parent-skill-root-router-template.md:20), which forecloses per-mode routers by authoring rule as well as by parser.
A routing shape must keep a hub-root ROUTER.md; RRC-001 fails without it.
